title: Pitts India Act, 1784
definition: A landmark constitutional reform enacted by the British Parliament to rectify the defects of the Regulating Act of 1773, establishing a system of 'Dual Control' (Diarchy) over the East India Company's affairs in India.
importanceInUpsc: It marks the beginning of British government control over the Company's administration, a recurring theme in the evolution of the Indian Constitution and administrative history.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Pitts India Act.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: East India Company's commercial vs political functions
